edit.description: widen the tests/ half of the spec locator scan to rootless filenames; retire the doc comment's park

summary: Widen the spec test-cite needle past its tests/ root to a bare *.test.ts filename, leaving the lane's glob

per.section: A claim names behavior, never location

tests: the test-cite needle flags a bare `Dispatcher.test.ts` filename carrying no root
pins: the test-cite needle leaves the `*.integration.test.ts` lane convention unflagged
no spec page cites a bare test filename
acceptance: the widened needle is green over the corpus, and the needle's doc comment no longer parks the rootless half as a human question
notes: Grammar ruled (inbox, 2026-09-11, operator): `*.integration.test.ts` is the lane's marker, so the needle matches a concrete filename and leaves the glob. Green today — `spec/worktrees.md`'s last rootless site was rewritten — and the doc comment deferring the rootless half to a human is expired narration, retired in the same commit. Reverted 9e9b326 is a working implementation. The needle now lives in `tests/helpers/specLocators.ts`, so `tests[]` goes red on the base.

edit.description: read a single-line doc block's orphan id off its own opener

summary: orphanedBlocks degrades a single-line doc block's id to the empty string; read the id off the opener instead
tests: the orphan scan identifies a single-line doc block by its own text
acceptance: an injected single-line orphan comes back keyed by its text, and two such orphans in one file are two distinct ALLOWED_ORPHANS keys
notes: A single-line block closes on its own opener, so the first-content-line slice is empty and the id falls to `<path>: ` — a placeholder standing in for content that failed to resolve. ALLOWED_ORPHANS is empty today, so the leak is latent: an allowlisted single-line grant would cover any later single-line orphan in the same file. `orphanedBlocks` now lives in `tests/helpers/docAgreement.ts`, so the 4dbfc07 wall (fix riding forward inside the suite file) is gone.

edit.description: expose the nested-`describe` reader the depth bound rests on; shrink the bound's doc comment to a pointer at it
pin the depth bound beside the extraction scan, with a nested-`describe` sample as its sensitivity control

summary: declaredGrammar's column-0-or-2 bound rests on an unchecked precondition — pin that the suite nests no `describe`

per.section: Narration is the ladder's bottom rung

pins: the extraction scan's depth bound holds — the retired-narration suite declares every `describe` at the top level
acceptance: a nested `describe` sample fails the new pin, and the bound's doc comment points at the pin instead of asserting the condition itself
notes: Build's note on the extraction: indentation is the proxy for `outside an it body`, so a nested `describe` puts its scanners at column 4 and the extraction scan reads them as `it`-local drivers — going quiet on exactly the residue it exists to catch. Not vacuous today (19 top-level describes, none nested), but Agent/chain/Dispatcher suites all nest, so the shape is routine here. An AST reader is the rung above; a checkable precondition is the cheap one.
